headline: Massachusetts opens applications for $1 million cell phone-free school grants
dek: Public school districts, charter schools and collaboratives can seek funding for policies, training and equipment, with applications due Oct. 21.
body: Massachusetts opened applications Thursday for $1 million in competitive grants intended to help schools reduce student cell phone use and create more focused learning environments, the Healey-Driscoll administration announced.

Public school districts, charter schools and educational collaboratives are eligible to apply. The money can support policy development and implementation, staff training, professional learning, lockable phone storage and other tools that help schools limit device access during the school day.

The cell phone-free program is part of a broader $4.5 million Student Support and Wellbeing Systems grant opportunity administered by the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education. Districts can receive base funding of up to $50,000 and may request an additional $10,000 to $20,000 for cell phone-free activities, depending on enrollment.

Applications must move through the state’s Grants for Education Management System and receive superintendent or chief executive approval by 5 p.m. Oct. 21. DESE says priority for the cell phone-free component will go to applicants that do not already have related equipment, training or prior grant support.
